title: Intelligent ingest proxy for live console telemetry
creator: Rohan Patel
description: Build a lightweight, horizontally-scalable ingest proxy that fronts the real-time console metrics pipeline. The proxy will accept telemetry events (usage, latencies, errors, traces) from the Console UI/agents, perform validation/enrichment, and route events into the low-latency hot path or a cost-optimized cold path depending on tenant SLOs and event type. Goals: reduce end-to-end ingest latency for high-SLO customers, bound resource usage for noisy tenants, and add a single place for early schema validation, sampling, and hot-key mitigation before events hit downstream stream processors.
accepted_criteria: Proxy accepts Console metric events over HTTP/HTTP2 and gRPC with <25ms median processing latency in canary
Per-tenant policy evaluation (route-to-hot vs cold) applied in proxy and enforced for 100% of canary traffic
Hot-key detection triggers adaptive sampling or rekeying to avoid shard imbalance under synthetic 10x skew tests
Events failing schema validation are rejected with a clear error code and written to a per-tenant dead-letter topic
End-to-end tests demonstrating graceful fallback: when hot path is congested, proxy redirects to cold path and emits observability events
Canary rollout plan documented and automated via feature flag gating and weighted traffic shifting
design_decisions: Architecture: stateless ingest proxy + local LRU policy cache; stateful decisions (long-term tenant profiles) read from a fast key-value store (Dynamo/Redis) to avoid central bottlenecks
Transport: support both HTTP/1.1+JSON and gRPC/protobuf for internal clients; use binary protobuf on hot path to minimize cpu/serde time
Partitioning: dynamic partition key selection (tenant_id + adaptive_hash) when hot-key skew detected; proxy performs mutable rekey hints rather than mutating downstream topology
Sampling: two-stage sampling. Fast path uses deterministic per-tenant sampling rates; under overload, escalate to statistically unbiased reservoir sampling at proxy
Exactly-once vs at-least-once: prioritize low-latency and simple idempotency via event dedup token (idempotency key) emitted to downstream processors; full exactly-once reserved for future work
Backpressure: implement token-bucket admission per-tenant and global concurrency limits; on overrun, proxy returns 429 + retry-after and emits quota-denied telemetry
Schema validation: use JSON schema v7 for public events and protobuf for internal hot-path schema to enable faster parse and earlier failures
Observability: produce structured trace/span for each request that includes policy decision and final route (hot/cold/dropped) and expose metrics for per-tenant latency, sampling rate, and rejections
tasks: Create proxy service skeleton (HTTP + gRPC) and deploy to dev cluster
Implement schema validation and dead-letter sink integration
Integrate tenant policy store and local caching with TTL; add admin API to update policies
Implement adaptive partition key generator and hot-key detector based on recent request distribution
Add admission control (token-bucket) per-tenant and global quota enforcement
Wire proxy to hot-path binary topic and cold-path compressed S3-backed topic with appropriate headers
Add tracing/instrumentation, dashboards (p50/p95/p99), and alerting for proxy errors and routing ratios
Create canary pipeline: feature flag, gradual rollout, and automated rollback on error budget burn
End-to-end integration tests including synthetic hotspot and failover scenarios
Prepare runbook for incidents and document expected observability signatures for common failure modes
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created by Rohan. Initial proposal discussed in infra sync. Decided to prototype as separate service to avoid large changes to existing stream processors.
2025-02-18: Spike completed. Prototype proxy (go) demonstrates <20ms per-request baseline for protobuf path. Found Redis TTL churn under load; moving to local LRU cache with async refresh.
2025-02-24: Design review with PM/Observability. Agreed on two-stage sampling and to emit detailed policy-decision traces. Assigned Maya to implement core proxy work.

2025-02-28: Implemented schema validation and dead-letter write path to topic 'console-ingest-deadletter'. Unit tests added. Observed 3% of events rejected in dev due to legacy UI format — flagged to frontend team.
2025-03-01: Hot-key detector algorithm (exponential decay frequency sketch) landed on branch; initial bench shows stable detection at 10x skew. Added rekey hint header 'X-Redwood-Rekey'.

2025-03-04: Canary deployment started for 5% of internal staging cluster traffic. Median proxy latency 22ms, p99 75ms. One tenant exceeded token-bucket and received 429s; policy updated to increase quota for that tenant during canary.
